label: Born at Merchiston Castle
description: John Napier was born in the medieval tower house of Merchiston Castle.

sources.quote: John Napier was born in the medieval tower house of Merchiston Castle in 1550, the exact date of his birth is unknown.

label: Enrolled at University of St Andrews
description: John Napier enrolled at the University of St Andrews where he attended St. Salvator's College.

sources.quote: In 1563 John Napier, aged thirteen, enrolled at the University of St Andrews where he attended St. Salvator's College and lodged with the college's principal, John Rutherford.

label: Mother Janet Bothwell died
description: John Napier experienced the tragedy of the sudden loss of his mother within three months of beginning his studies.

sources.quote: Within three months of beginning his studies, John Napier experienced the tragedy of the sudden loss of his mother.

label: Left for Europe
description: John Napier left the university prematurely and travelled to continental Europe.

sources.quote: Historians tend to agree that he left from Leith for Europe in 1564 to continue his studies, but his destination uncertain.

label: Returned to Scotland
description: John Napier returned to Scotland aged twenty-one years.

sources.quote: Historians generally agree that John Napier returned to Scotland in 1571, aged twenty-one years.

label: Married Elizabeth Stirling
description: John and Elizabeth Napier married and took up residence in Gartness, Stirlingshire.

sources.quote: John and Elizabeth Napier married and took up residence in Gartness, Stirlingshire in 1573, where a new home was built which included a spacious garden and orchard.

label: Son Archibald born
description: Their son Archibald was born at Gartness.

sources.quote: Their son Archibald was born at Gartness in 1576 and a daughter, Jane, soon followed.

label: Elizabeth Stirling died
description: Elizabeth Napier sadly died, aged just twenty-seven years old.

sources.quote: Elizabeth Napier sadly died in 1579, aged just twenty-seven years old.

label: Married Agnes Chisholm
description: John Napier remarried within a few years of Elizabeth's death.

sources.quote: Within a few years, John Napier remarried and had five sons and daughters with his new wife, Agnes Chisholm, daughter of Sir James Chisholm of Cromlix.

label: Published Plaine Discovery
description: John Napier's long-held interest in the subject of religious apocalypse culminated in the publication of Plaine Discovery.

sources.quote: John Napier's long-held interest in the subject of religious apocalypse culminated in the publication of Plaine Discovery of the Whole Revelation of St John in 1593.

label: Submitted war inventions
description: He submitted a list of inventions to the Government titled Secrett inventionis.

sources.quote: He submitted a list of inventions to the Government titled Secrett inventionis, profitabill and necessary in the defence of this lland, and withstanding Strangers, enemies of God's truth and religion in 1596.

label: Published Mirifici Logarithmorum Canonis Descriptio
description: John Napier published Mirifici Logarithmorum Canonis Descriptio which included ninety pages of logarithmic tables.

sources.quote: John Napier published Mirifici Logarithmorum Canonis Descriptio in 1614, which included ninety pages of logarithmic tables as well as thirty-seven pages of instruction to make the process of carrying out long, complicated calculations easier.

label: Henry Briggs visited Napier
description: Henry Briggs travelled from London to Edinburgh to visit John Napier.

sources.quote: Having read Mirifici Logarithmorum Canonis Descriptio Henry Briggs, Professor of Mathematics at Gresham College, travelled from London to Edinburgh to visit John Napier in 1615.

label: Published Rabdologiae
description: John Napier published Rabdologiae as a means to assist in making mathematics accessible to wider audiences.

sources.quote: John Napier published Rabdologiae in 1617 as a means to assist in making mathematics accessible to wider audiences.
It is widely reported that John Napier experienced poor health for a number of years prior to his death on 04 April 1617, and it is suspected that he suffered significantly from gout.

label: Published Constructio
description: John Napier's logarithmic methodology was published by his son, Robert.

sources.quote: John Napier's logarithmic methodology was published in 1619 by his son, Robert, which was titled Constructio.

label: Published De Arte Logistica
description: Napier's mathematical notes were published by his descendant, Mark Napier.

sources.quote: Robert also collected many of his father's mathematical notes and papers, which were later published under the title De Arte Logistica by his descendant, Mark Napier, in 1839.

label: Merchiston Tower saved
description: Merchiston Tower was saved from demolition and integrated as part of a campus.

sources.quote: Merchiston Tower was saved from demolition in 1958, restored and integrated as part of a campus for a new college named after John Napier.

label: Napier Technical College opened
description: Napier Technical College opened its doors to 800 students.

sources.quote: In 1964, Napier Technical College opened its doors to 800 students which offered courses including coppering, cabinet making, boat building, chemistry and engineering.
